name: Dowagiac Area History Museum
what: A free museum with about 6,000 square feet of exhibits on the history of Dowagiac, Cass County and the surrounding area, including the Round Oak stove story and an Orphan Train exhibit.
research: Online collections database; ask the museum about research use (269-783-2560, info@dowagiacmuseum.info).
note: Hours Tue–Fri 10–5, Sat 10–2. It took over from the former Southwestern Michigan College Museum.

name: Dowagiac District Library – Genealogy & Local History
what: The public library for Dowagiac, with books, microfilm and digital resources for genealogy and local history.
research: Questions to genealogy@dowagiacdl.org.
note: Mon/Wed/Fri 9–5:30, Tue/Thu 9–7, Sat 9–2.

name: Bonine House
what: A restored nineteenth-century home in Vandalia, open as a museum with docent-led visits. It tells the story of Cass County's part in the Underground Railroad, and its seasonal events include a Christmas open house.
note: Open May–October, Mon–Fri 2–5 pm; private tours by arrangement through the operator's contact page. The operator's site name includes 'Underground Railroad' (see report).
hours: May to October, Mon–Fri 2–5 pm; private tours by arrangement.

name: Pioneer Log Cabin Museum
what: A log cabin museum in Cassopolis, kept by volunteers, holding pioneer-era objects from Cass County.
note: URL supplied by the site owner, but the site blocks automated fetching (robots rule), so I could not confirm it loads. The Village of Cassopolis parks page confirms the address and says the museum is 'periodically open'; there are no set hours.
hours: Open at times through the season; see the museum’s website.

name: Newton House
what: A historic farmhouse museum with permanent and changing displays on daily life from 1844 to 1930, when the Newton family lived there.
research: Several rooms are set aside for reading and research on the family, the surrounding woods and local history; it also keeps documents, family histories and artifacts.
note: Open houses on the first Sunday of each month, June–September, 1:00–4:30 pm. Owned by MSU and leased to Cass County; MSU trustees approved a sale to the Cass County Historical Society in June 2026, and I could not confirm whether the sale has closed.
hours: Open houses on the first Sunday of each month, June to September, 1:00–4:30 pm.

name: Cass County Historical Society
what: The county historical society. It runs the Newton House museum together with the county and publishes books on Cass County history.
research: Its publications are sold through the Cass District Library Local History Branch.
note: No public office address; email ccmihistoricalsociety@gmail.com.

name: Cass District Library – Local History Branch
what: A branch library given over to Cass County history and genealogy.
research: Plat maps, county newspapers on microfilm (Cassopolis, Dowagiac, Edwardsburg, Marcellus, Niles titles), obituary indexes 1998–2025, marriage, death and divorce records on microfilm, cemetery and rural-school guides, yearbooks and a vertical file.
note: Mon–Thu 9–4; closed Fri–Sun. Phone 269-357-7823.

name: Edwardsburg Area History Museum
what: A community history museum in a donated house on Main Street, with displays and talks on Edwardsburg-area history.
research: Contact the museum about research (269-663-3005, edwardsburgmuseum@yahoo.com).
note: Open mid-April to mid-December; Tue–Fri 1–4, Sat 11–2.

name: Fort St. Joseph Museum (Niles History Center)
what: A free city museum in the former carriage house of the Chapin Mansion, telling Niles history from earliest times through the railroad, business and industrial eras, including Civil War and military service.
research: Ask the Assistant Director about collections access (mwatson@nilesmi.org, 269-845-4054 ext. 4013).
note: Wed–Fri 10–4, Sat 10–3. The first floor is being updated while the museum stays open.

name: Historic Chapin Mansion
what: A Victorian-era mansion run by the Niles History Center and shown on docent-led tours.
note: 2026 tours Fridays and Saturdays at 1 pm through December, starting at the museum; $5 adults, 18 and under free; first floor ADA accessible.

name: Niles Historic Sites (Four Flags City)
what: Historic places around Niles listed by the city, including the Four Flags Hotel, the Niles rail depot, the site of Fort St. Joseph and Silverbrook Cemetery.
address: Various locations, Niles, MI (e.g. Fort St. Joseph site at Bond and Fort Streets; Four Flags Hotel at 4th and Main)
note: Mostly outdoor or exterior sites; the hotel and depot are working buildings, not museums.
hours: Mostly outdoor sites; the hotel and depot are working buildings.

name: Niles District Library – Local History & Genealogy
what: The public library for Niles, with local newspaper and genealogy resources.
research: Digitized Niles Daily Star from 1887 (in-library), obituary lookup service, Ancestry Library Edition, MyHeritage and American Ancestors.
address: 620 E. Main St., Niles, MI 49120 (entrance on Cedar St.)
note: Mon–Thu 9–8, Fri–Sat 10–6. Not to be confused with Niles-Maine District Library in Illinois.

name: History Center at Courthouse Square (Berrien County Historical Association)
what: The county historical association's museum campus around the 1839 courthouse, with the sheriff's residence, a pioneer log cabin and a working blacksmith forge open for exhibits and programs.
research: The association's research library and offices are in the upper floors of the sheriff's residence; contact ahead (269-471-1202, info@berrienhistory.org).
address: 313 N. Cass St., Berrien Springs, MI 49103
note: Museum buildings Wed–Sun 10–5; $5 admission. The official home page still shows 2017 hours, and current hours come from the county community directory. Closed during the Youth Fair and over the winter holidays.

name: Morton House Museum
what: A historic house museum billed as 'The Home of Benton Harbor History,' with exhibits, talks and tours.
research: Research room visits by appointment.
note: Open Wednesdays and Saturdays 11–2; tours by appointment.

name: North Berrien Historical Museum
what: A free museum on the history of northern Berrien County and its buildings, run by the North Berrien Historical Society.
research: Has a local history section; it also offers film and slide digitizing. Contact ahead.
note: Tue–Fri 10–4; groups call two weeks ahead.

name: Pears Mill
what: An 1857 water-powered flour and grist mill, the only survivor of thirteen mills that once stood on McCoy Creek, run by volunteers of the Buchanan Preservation Society.
address: Downtown Buchanan, south of Front Street between Oak St. and Days Ave., Buchanan, MI
note: Saturdays 9–1, Memorial Day to Labor Day; free; group tours by arrangement.

name: Fort Miami Heritage Society Archive
what: The archive of the society that ran the Heritage Museum and Cultural Center in St. Joseph from 1997 to 2025, holding thousands of documents and photographs on St. Joseph, Benton Harbor and the area.
research: Research requests by email (info@fortmiamiheritage.org); the online catalog can be browsed.
address: 777 Riverview Drive, Suite 109D, Benton Harbor, MI 49022
note: The former St. Joseph museum is permanently closed. There are no posted public hours, so contact the society before visiting.
hours: No posted public hours: write to the society before visiting.

name: Berrien County Genealogical Society
what: The county genealogical society, with regular meetings and online Berrien County and cemetery records.
research: Online records (some members-only).
address: P.O. Box 8808, Benton Harbor, MI 49023 (mailing, per a third-party listing)
note: The site is active (2026) but gives no street address or meeting place; email info@bcgensoc.com.

name: Van Buren County Historical Society Museum
what: The county museum in the former county poorhouse, with displays filling 44 rooms on four floors, plus a log cabin and outdoor exhibits.
research: Holds historical documents; ask about access (269-500-1450).
note: Wed, Fri and Sun noon–5; guided tours on Sundays, other days by appointment.

name: Toni I. Benson Room of Local History and Genealogy (Van Buren District Library)
what: A local history and genealogy room in the Webster Memorial Branch, covering southwestern Michigan.
research: Books, microfilm (Bangor, Decatur, Paw Paw and South Haven newspapers), the Southwest Michigan Obituary index (89,000+ entries), plat books from 1860, family files, yearbooks, cemetery books and a one-room-school collection.
note: Mon–Fri 10–4, Sat 9–3.

name: Van Buren Regional Genealogical Society
what: A genealogical society serving Van Buren and neighbouring counties, with a reference collection that is free to the public.
research: In-library-use collection at the Hartford Public Library.
address: Hartford Public Library, 12 Church St., Hartford, MI 49057 (mail: P.O. Box 234)
note: Collection hours not listed; check with the Hartford Public Library.
hours: Ask the Hartford Public Library for collection hours.

name: Michigan Maritime Museum
what: A museum of Michigan's maritime history, with exhibits, a boat-building workshop, historic and replica vessels and a Coast Guard boathouse.
research: The site lists a maritime research library; that page would not load for me.
note: Hours are on its Hours & Admissions page (not seen).

name: Liberty Hyde Bailey Museum & Gardens
what: The 1850s boyhood home of horticulturist Liberty Hyde Bailey, one of South Haven's oldest houses, with gardens, a smokehouse, a blacksmith shop and a short nature trail.
address: 903 S. Bailey Ave., South Haven, MI 49090
note: Saturdays 11–5; season not stated. City-owned, run by a nonprofit.

name: Historical Association of South Haven
what: The local historical association, based in the Hartman School building, collecting photos, books and artifacts on South Haven history.
research: Research library of photos and materials; ask about access.
address: Hartman School, 355 Hubbard Street, South Haven, MI 49090
note: Building open Tue and Wed 9–3. I could not confirm a public exhibit space.

name: Michigan Flywheelers Museum
what: An outdoor and indoor museum of antique farm engines and machinery, with a sawmill, a shingle mill, a 1920s-style 'Olde Town' and a small railroad.
note: Hours are on its tours page (not seen); mostly seasonal events.
hours: Mostly seasonal events; see their website.

name: St. Joseph County Historical Society of Michigan (headquarters and archives)
what: The county historical society, with headquarters and research archives on St. Joseph County history, a downtown building-history walking tour and the White Pigeon Land Office.
research: Archives with obituaries, wills, land records, directories, photographs and one-room-school records; archivists help researchers.
address: 34 N. Main St., Three Rivers, MI 49093
note: Fridays 10–4 or by appointment; 269-273-6003.

name: White Pigeon Prairie U.S. Land Office
what: A state and national historic site and the only standing land office of its era in the Midwest (1831–34), with surveying equipment, maps and exhibits.
address: 113 W. Chicago Rd., White Pigeon, MI 49099
note: Summer open houses 1–4 pm; group tours by arrangement (269-718-7013).

name: Sturgis Historical Museum at the Depot
what: A local history museum in the Sturgis railroad depot, with a model train room and gift shop.
research: The White Glove Room holds yearbooks, city and county directories and a reference collection; by appointment (269-503-7440).
note: Hours not listed on the page; call ahead.

name: Three Rivers Public Library – Michigan Room
what: The library's local history and genealogy room for Three Rivers and St. Joseph County.
research: Census and genealogy materials, war records, cemetery records, city directories, high school yearbooks and a digital newspaper archive; for use in the room only.
address: 88 N. Main St., Three Rivers, MI 49093
note: Open whenever the library is open; staff cannot do lengthy research.

name: The History Museum
what: The regional history museum for the St. Joseph River Valley, with changing exhibits, the Oliver Mansion, a worker's home and a pioneer cabin on its campus.
research: Archive of about 600,000 items collected since 1867, partly searchable online; ask about research visits (574-235-9664).
address: 808 W. Washington Street, South Bend, IN 46601
note: Mon–Sat 10–5, Sun 12–5.

name: Oliver Mansion (Copshaholm)
what: A furnished Gilded Age mansion on The History Museum's campus, shown on guided tours.
address: 808 W. Washington Street, South Bend, IN 46601
note: Guided tours twice daily; times not listed.
hours: Guided tours twice a day; see the museum’s site for times.

name: Studebaker National Museum
what: A museum of the Studebaker company and its vehicles, with permanent and changing exhibitions.
research: Has archives and a photo archive, plus a 'Research Your Studebaker' service; contact the museum about access.
note: Mon–Sat 10–5, Sun 12–5.

name: St. Joseph County Public Library – Local & Family History
what: A local and family history department on the third floor of the Main Library.
research: Newspapers in print and microfilm, clipping files, church records, yearbooks, an obituary index and archival collections in closed stacks; librarian consultations and digitization stations.
address: 304 S. Main St., South Bend, IN 46601
note: Mon–Thu 9–7, Fri–Sat 9–5, Sun 1–5 (Labor Day to Memorial Day). Contact ahead for archival items.

name: Mishawaka-Penn-Harris Public Library – Local & Family History
what: A local and family history department on the lower level of the Mishawaka Library, covering Mishawaka, Penn and Harris Townships, St. Joseph County and nearby counties.
research: Print, digital and archival materials, microfilm reader and the Mishawaka Memories digital archive.
note: Open during library hours.

name: Mishawaka Historical Museum
what: A museum of Mishawaka history with artifacts, photographs and programs.
note: Hours not listed on the site; 574-217-8807.

name: Historic New Carlisle
what: A local historical society with an office, a small museum and a gift shop, offering exhibits, walking tours and preservation work.
address: 112 E. Michigan Street, New Carlisle, IN 46552
note: Hours not listed; 574-654-3897.

name: South Bend Area Genealogical Society
what: An active genealogical society with programs and online indexes for St. Joseph County records.
research: Online indexes (marriages, naturalizations, doctor and midwife licences and others).
note: Contact through its website.

name: St. Joseph County Archives & Records Center
what: The county's archives and records centre, holding historic county records such as marriages, wills, naturalizations and burial permits.
research: All record requests go through the centre (574-235-9091, archives@sjcindiana.com).
address: 1140 S. Lafayette Blvd., South Bend, IN
note: The county page blocks automated fetching. Address and hours (Mon–Fri 8–4:30) come from SBAGS.

name: IU South Bend Archives and Special Collections
what: The university's archives and special collections at the Franklin D. Schurz Library, about 1,500 cubic feet of records.
research: Open to the public; call or email ahead (574-520-4410).
address: Franklin D. Schurz Library, IU South Bend, South Bend, IN
note: Collecting scope and street address not stated on the page.

name: IU South Bend Civil Rights Heritage Center
what: A university centre in the former Engman Public Natatorium with a permanent exhibit on the pool's history, plus public talks and programs.
research: Collects oral histories and documents with the Schurz Library.
note: Public hours not listed.

name: University of Notre Dame Archives
what: The university's archives, holding university records, manuscripts, publications and Catholic history collections.
research: Reading room open weekdays 9:30–4:30; contact ahead, since many collections are kept off site.
address: Hesburgh Library, University of Notre Dame, Notre Dame, IN
note: Mainly about Notre Dame and Catholic history, with little local history.

name: Elkhart County Historical Museum
what: The county history museum, run with Elkhart County Parks, holding over 30,000 artifacts spanning about 12,000 years of local history.
research: Research library with photos, diaries, family records, plat maps and census lists; appointments recommended (research@elkhartcountyhistory.org).
note: Tue–Sat 9–5; free.

name: Ruthmere
what: A 1910 Beaux-Arts mansion with original furnishings and decorative arts, shown on guided tours.
address: 302 E. Beardsley Ave., Elkhart, IN 46514 (tours start at the Beardsley Discovery Center, 819 N. Main St.)
note: Tours Tue–Sat 10–3 hourly, Sun 1–3; closed Jan 1–Mar 31.

name: Havilah Beardsley House
what: The 1848 home of Elkhart's founding family, shown on guided tours with exhibits.
note: Same tour schedule and season as Ruthmere; first floor wheelchair accessible.

name: Goshen Historical Society Museum
what: A free downtown museum on Goshen's history, with exhibits and local history books.
research: Contact the museum (574-975-0033).
note: Tue–Sat 10–4; first Fridays until 8.

name: Goshen Public Library – Indiana Room
what: The library's local history and genealogy collection.
research: Elkhart County vital-record indexes, Goshen newspapers on microfilm 1837–2022, Sanborn maps, plat books, city directories and yearbooks.
note: Address from a RootsWeb list, not the page itself.

name: Elkhart Public Library – Local History and Genealogy
what: The local history collection on the second floor of the Downtown Library.
research: Obituary and local history indexes, cemetery and funeral-home records, city directories, yearbooks and a photo archive.

name: Evelyn Lehman Culp Heritage Collection (Nappanee Center)
what: A local history museum and archive run with the Nappanee Public Library, with rotating exhibits on about 150 years of Nappanee history.
research: Heritage Collection database online; genealogy and local history services.
note: Mon–Fri 9–5, Sat 9–1.

name: National New York Central Railroad Museum
what: A city-run railroad museum on Elkhart's rail history, with exhibits and locomotives.
note: Wed–Sat 10–5.

name: RV/MH Hall of Fame and Museum
what: A museum of the history of recreational vehicles and manufactured housing, with vintage RVs.
note: Apr 1–Nov 1: Mon–Sat 9–5, Sun 10–3. Address from Wikipedia.

name: Bonneyville Mill
what: A county park around a historic grist mill that still grinds flour, with trails along the river.
note: Mill open Tue–Sun 10–5, Apr 14–Nov 15.

name: Mennonite Historical Library (Goshen College)
what: A major research library on Anabaptist, Mennonite and Amish history, with Goshen College history materials.
research: Off-campus researchers should contact staff before visiting.
address: Good Library, 3rd floor, Goshen College, 1700 S. Main St., Goshen, IN 46526
note: Mon–Fri 8–5. Its scope is religious history, not county history.
hours: Mon–Fri 8–5. Its subject is Anabaptist and Mennonite history.

name: WMU Archives & Regional History Collections (Zhang Legacy Collections Center)
what: Western Michigan University's regional archive, holding papers, newspapers, photographs and township and county records for southwest Michigan, including Berrien, Cass, St. Joseph and Van Buren.
research: Material used on site; email arch-collect@wmich.edu with research questions.
note: Outside the six counties. County coverage taken from a RootsWeb wiki page; hours on WMU LibCal.
hours: In Kalamazoo, just outside the valley; hours on the WMU library site.
